gui.dndsheets.guide.cat.character.desc: The sheet, levelling up, resting and dropping to 0.
gui.dndsheets.guide.cat.dm.desc: Panel, wands, monsters, dungeons and your own content.
gui.dndsheets.guide.landing: Everything this mod does, in parts. If you have never played D&D, start with "First game": it explains the game, not just the buttons. The rest reads in any order, and here it is searchable.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.advantage_basic: With advantage you roll two d20 and keep the better one; with disadvantage, the worse. It is how the game rewards a good idea or punishes bad footing, and they come up on their own: someone helping you, darkness, being grappled. You never ask for them, the mod applies them.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.characters: You can keep several characters. Open /dndchar to switch, create or delete. Each one has its own level, hit points, inventory, spells and resources: switching puts the previous one’s gear away and brings out theirs, nothing is lost.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.class_items: Your DM may hand you a class-resource item (Rage Totem, Second Wind, Bardic Inspiration Horn, Wild Shape token, Metamagic charm, Divine Smite gauntlet, Hunter's Mark arrow, Shield, Counterspell rune...). Right-click it to use that feature.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.compendium: The compendium is the manual inside the game: /dndcompendium opens the lists of loaded spells, monsters, magic items and weapons, with their rules. You do not need to be a DM or know any id. Not to be confused with your Spellbook, which only shows the spells YOUR character knows.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.cover: Standing behind something counts. A half-height block between you and the shooter gives half cover (+2 AC and Dexterity saves); nearly covered, three-quarters (+5). Nothing to switch on: it is measured against the blocks actually in the way.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.d20: Almost everything resolves the same way: roll 1d20, add the modifier your sheet shows, and compare it to a difficulty the DM sets. 10 is easy, 15 average, 20 hard. Match it or beat it and you succeed. The dice buttons on your sheet already add the modifier for you.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.death_saves: At 0 HP you roll death saves. 3 successes stabilizes you, 3 failures means death, and a natural 20 wakes you up. A nearby player can also revive you.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.distance: Type /dnddistance followed by a target's name to check the distance to them in feet.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_bind: The other way round too: build the NPC wherever it is best built — an NPC mod gives you skins, poses, dialogs and objectives this mod does not have — then right-click it with the DM Wand. A list of the whole bestiary opens; whichever you pick sticks to it.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_bind_2: From then on it has AC, HP, resistances, attacks and a turn of its own like any monster. Its AI is left alone, so is any name it already had, and so is any gear slot the stat block does not mention. By command it is /dndmonsters bind, and bind clear undoes it.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_bosses: Bestiary bosses play like bosses: adult and ancient dragons, the lich and the tarrasque have Legendary Resistance (three failed saves a day they decide to pass) and multiattack.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_bosses_2: They also have legendary actions: they strike at the end of someone else's turn. All three are declared in the monster JSON with legendaryResistances, legendaryActions and multiattack.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_commands_2: Any player can use /roll, /rollprivate, /dnddistance, /dndguide and /dndcompendium, plus /dndchar, /dndjournal and /dnditems except for their DM subcommands. Everything else needs operator permission.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_content_pack: Custom weapons, spells, monsters and presets are JSON files in <world>/dndsheets/{weapons,spells,monsters,presets}/. An English pack works the same: "fire" and "fuego" are one damage type as far as resistances are concerned.

You do not have to write outside content by hand: tools/import_srd.py converts the SRD (5.1 and 5.2) and community packs (Open5e) into the mod's format, and only ADDS — it never overwrites what you already have.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_creatures: Every monster declares a creature type (undead, fiend, beast...). Real rules hang off it: Divine Smite adds a die against undead and fiends, and Hold Person only affects humanoids. A monster with no type is outside those rules, for better and worse.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_dungeons_1: Dungeons: build a room, save it with a structure block (SAVE), then right-click that block with the DM Wand to capture it as a piece, pre-filled. Golden rule: a start pool may only hold pieces that carry the start jigsaw.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_dungeons_2: Configure each jigsaw block with a right-click (sneak+click copies its config to another), then generate from DM Panel (P) > Dungeons > Generate dungeon. A new or edited pool does NOT show up on /reload: it is worldgen. Leave the world and come back in.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_dungeons_3: You do not have to build every room. Drop an .nbt structure into the game's dndsheets/structures/ folder and use /dnddungeon import "<file>": it pastes it where you stand and tells you how many jigsaws it carries.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_dungeons_4: If it carries none, place them with the DM Wand and capture it as a room of your own. If it already has them, /dnddungeon import "<file>" pool <pool> registers it as a piece directly.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_dungeons_5: No DM at the table: with solo mode on (/dndsolo), anyone can generate one — you don't need to be an operator. And you no longer have to populate it by hand: every generated dungeon already comes with its own monsters in several rooms, scaled to the world's difficulty (/difficulty).
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_encounters: An encounter is a group of monsters saved under a name. Prepare it before the session in the DM Panel (Create content > Encounters) by writing "dndsheets:goblin x4, dndsheets:wolf x2".
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_encounters_2: Drop the whole thing with /dndencounters spawn <id>, or at coordinates if you want it set up on the other side of the door. They come out spread in a circle, and initiative starts on its own with the first hit.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_first_1: To run the game you need to be an operator of the world: the P key opens the DM Panel, and without permission it does nothing. The rest is yours — the mod carries the rules and the numbers, but the story, the map and what waits behind the door are on you.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_first_2: A first session that works: have every player bring a set-up character, prepare ONE room and ONE small encounter, describe where they are, let them talk, and when someone attacks initiative starts on its own. Half an hour is plenty for the first one.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_first_3: A campaign is sessions strung together in the same world. Between them, a long rest restores everything. Keep your notes and handouts in the journal (/dndjournal) instead of relying on memory, and prepare encounters before you sit down: it shows at the table.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_journal: The campaign journal is your handouts: write in a Book and Quill and publish it with /dndjournal publish "<title>". share <id> <players> hands it to just those players, party <id> makes it public to the table, and hide <id> makes it private again. Plain /dndjournal opens it: everyone sees their own.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_more_packs: /dndweapons and /dndpresets load custom weapon and class-preset JSON packs; /dndtraits loads and grants passive traits; /dndoptions loads the race/background/class picker lists.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_notes: /dndnotes give <players> hands out a DM Notebook: a renamed Book and Quill. It's private like any book, and Minecraft saves its contents on its own.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_npc_ai: Monsters and NPCs are spawned frozen: the DM drives them. With "ai": true in the monster JSON they keep their base entity's own AI alive, which is what makes an NPC mod's entities useful (patrolling, following the party, holding a post). For an NPC with a sheet: /dndchar spawn <id> <entity> true.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_npc_ai_2: In combat the mod still rules: entering turn mode switches that AI off and gives it back when the fight ends, so the creature resolves its turn by 5e rules and does not wander through the encounter out of turn. The AI is for outside combat, which is where there was nothing.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_ownclock: Some bosses do not queue. With “ownClock”: true in its JSON, the creature leaves the turn ORDER but not the fight: it acts on its own every 6 seconds (one 5e round), moves freely and waits for no one. The 10 ancient dragons, the tarrasque, the lich, the kraken and the solar ship marked already.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_ownclock_2: It is not “no rules”, it is “no queue”: it takes damage by every rule, it counts towards the fight ending, and paralysing or stunning it stops it dead. It loses its legendary actions (it no longer needs them) and neither gives nor takes opportunity attacks. The table gets an on-screen title so it reads as deliberate.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_panel: Press P (requires operator permission) to open the DM Panel: turns, spawn NPCs/monsters, grant traits, give items/weapons/spells, adjust a sheet, apply presets, dungeons, and create content — all without commands.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_sheet_admin: /dndsheet adjusts any player's sheet remotely: setslots, restkit, advantage, damagetype, gold, pact, setlevel, setac, setroll, plus the ...item subcommands (rageitem, secondwinditem, smiteitem...) that hand out class-resource items.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_turns: Run combat with /dndturns: start, next, cancel, end, and effect to apply a status effect to a player.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.dm_wand: Right-click a monster with the DM Wand to resolve its attacks and spells, or manage its custom attacks.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.first_combat: When combat starts, the DM opens turn mode and the chat tells you when it is your turn. On your turn you can move and do ONE thing: attack, cast a spell, dodge, dash or help someone. The moment you act, your turn ends. Outside combat you play normal Minecraft.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.first_ten: In order: 1) make your character — press H, "Characters", "Character setup...", and fill in the steps showing a dash. 2) check the Skills tab to see what you are good at. 3) ask your DM where the game starts. That is it: the rest you learn by playing.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.glossary_1: The words you will hear most. HP: your hit points, your life; at 0 you go down. AC: your armour class, how hard you are to hit — whoever attacks you rolls 1d20 and has to match or beat it. Modifier: the +2 or -1 each ability score adds.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.glossary_2: Saving throw: a roll to withstand something already happening to you, like dodging a fireball. Proficiency: if you are proficient at something you also add your proficiency bonus, which comes from your class and background. Condition: a state that changes your rules (blinded, grappled, frightened).
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.hud_states: Top left shows what is happening to you: in red your conditions (paralysed, restrained, frightened...), in amber what you are holding that changes your next roll (concentration, Inspiration die, armed Smite, advantage).
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.intro: This is D&D: one of you plays the DM, the one who narrates, and everyone else runs a character. The DM describes where you are and what happens; you say what you do. When something could go either way, a die is rolled. Minecraft is the table: the world, the rooms and the monsters you see.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.level_up: Levelling raises your hit points, proficiency and spell slots on its own. At levels 4, 8, 12, 16 and 19 you also choose an Ability Score Improvement: +2 to one or +1 to two. If you close that screen without choosing, /dndchar improve reopens it.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.level_up_2: At those same levels you can take a FEAT instead of the improvement; the button is on the same screen. Sixteen ship from the SRD: origin feats, fighting styles and Epic Boons, which only show up from level 19. Your DM can add more with a JSON file.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.level_up_3: If your DM grants you a level in ANOTHER class (/dndsheet multiclass), your sheet reads "Fighter 3 / Wizard 2": hit points use each class's die, and spell slots come from your caster level, not your total level.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.magic_items: A magic item with properties (resistances, bonuses, charges) does nothing until you attune to it: /dnditems attune <id>, and at most three at a time. /dnditems list and /dnditems info <id> tell you what is loaded and what it does; /dnditems unattune <id> drops it and frees the slot.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.private_rolls: Shift+click a dice button (or use /rollprivate, /rp) for a private roll: only you and any online DM see the result, for things like Stealth or Investigation.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.rest: Right-click a Rest Kit to propose a short or long rest. The rest only happens once everyone accepts.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.roles: The DM is not the enemy: they set the scenes, run the monsters and decide what calls for a roll. The mod hands them the tools, but the story is yours, and no mod carries that. Half the game is talking: say what you want to do and the DM will tell you whether to roll.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.rolling: Click the dice buttons on your sheet to roll, or type /roll (or /r) followed by dice notation, e.g. /roll 1d20+5.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.sheet: Press H to open your sheet. The first time it is blank, and everything missing is chosen in one place: "Characters" > "Character setup...". That screen lists the steps — race, class, background, skill proficiencies — and the ones showing a dash are the ones you still need.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.sheet_2: Class is picked through a preset: besides the name it writes your six ability scores, hit die, starting gear and class traits. Once no dash is left in that list, you are ready to play. The Main, Skills and Attacks tabs at the top switch pages.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.skills: Being proficient in a skill means adding your proficiency bonus to that roll. Open it from the sheet with "Characters" > "Skill proficiencies..." and tick yours; the sheet writes the roll for you. In 5e you get a few, chosen from your class and background, so ask your DM which ones are yours.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.spell_casting_t: A levelled spell takes a moment to come out. Magic gathers in your hands and the action bar shows the progress. Take damage and you must make a Constitution save (DC 10, or half the damage) or lose it, slot included. Moving or being knocked out loses it too. Your DM can turn this off.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.spell_prepare: You cast what you have PREPARED, not everything you know. Open your Grimoire (G), pick a spell, press Prepare. You can hold your casting ability modifier plus your level; cantrips never count, they are at will. Trying an unprepared spell costs you nothing: it is refused, not charged.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.spell_schools: Each spell belongs to one of the eight schools, and each looks and sounds different when cast. It changes no rule: it is there so you can tell a Revivify from a Fireball the moment someone starts casting. The school shows in your Grimoire, and the search box filters by it.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.spells: Open your Grimoire from the sheet to see known spells and slots. Look at a target and cast to use a spell. Shift+click an area-spell staff to preview the blast radius without casting it.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.subclass: When you reach the level your class asks for, you choose a subclass: Champion, Life Domain, Thief... It lives on the sheet under "Characters" > "Character setup..." > Subclass, and only lists the ones your class can take right now. The choice is permanent, like a warlock pact.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.turn_actions: Your turn can be spent on something other than attacking. With the Turn Actions item: Dodge (attacks against you have disadvantage), Dash (double movement) or Disengage (moving away provokes nothing). With the Help item, right-click an ally to give their next attack advantage.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.turns: In turn mode you get one action and your movement speed on your turn. Your turn ends automatically once you act.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.vision: If the DM turns on the vision rules (/dndvision), darkness counts: below light level 4 you are blinded, you attack with disadvantage and you are attacked with advantage.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.vision_2: With darkvision (dwarf, elf, half-elf, gnome, half-orc, tiefling) you see it as dim light, and holding a torch or a lantern counts as bright light.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.wildshape: Wild Shape: right-click your druid token and pick a beast from the bestiary. You really become it — you take its hit points, its AC, its Strength, Dexterity and Constitution, and its attack. Your Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma stay yours: the beast does not make you dumb.
gui.dndsheets.guide.page.wildshape_2: And you look like it, to yourself and to everyone else. It lasts 10 rounds, or until you click again. If the form drops to 0 HP you do not die: you return to your body with the hit points you had when you transformed, and the damage the beast took stays with the beast.
